findings: The circular oscillator graphic top-right is thin and slightly under-resolved — the dotted arc plus single blue dot reads more like a diagram sketch than a fully composed counterweight to the headline mass.
Deep in the page the density of small mono-annotated body blocks becomes relentless; some transitions between essay, table and index blur into an undifferentiated grey field.
The 'Threshold / 123' numeric block and the index rows lean on a fairly conventional ledger-table treatment that a competent template could approximate.
what_works: Editorial serif display ('No conductor. No score. One pulse.') with 'pulse' set in italic blue is a genuine typographic point of view — high-contrast serif against an all-caps mono utility voice, not the default sans.
Asymmetric hero: left-aligned headline with mono metadata rail and an off-axis pulse graphic anchoring the right — real compositional tension, no centered-tagline template.
Restrained cream/near-black palette governed by a single blue accent used sparingly (italic word, roman numeral XI, the interactive dots) rather than as garnish.
Drop cap, pull-quote in italic serif, roman-numeral index and the black interactive pendulum panel signal a living-document editorial system, not a SaaS feature grid.
A.reasoning: The page commits to an editorial art-organism identity: high-contrast serif display against mono utility labels, generous asymmetric composition, a single blue accent used with discipline, and living-document devices (drop caps, pull quotes, indexed epochs, interactive canvases). None of the cardinal slop states are present — no centered gradient hero, no three-card grid, no default sans. It loses points only for a somewhat sketchy hero graphic and long stretches of dense grey body/table content that flatten hierarchy below the fold.

findings: Hero uses off-axis circular diagram with thin blue traces and single pulsing dot instead of centered headline or gradient
Text blocks employ consistent left margin with thin blue vertical rule creating rhythmic vertical flow rather than default centering
Interactive pendulum demo and case-study grid with small circular thumbnails avoid feature-card template entirely
what_works: Hero composition pairs large editorial text with asymmetric line-and-dot graphic that establishes the entrainment theme immediately
Pendulum simulation and numbered lockings list function as living instruments rather than static decoration
B.reasoning: Desktop screenshot shows a single decisive focal hierarchy in the hero with the circular trace graphic and stacked headline; spacing follows visible vertical rhythm without arbitrary gaps; color is limited to one blue accent used functionally for rules and highlights; no centered symmetry, no purple gradients, no three-card row, and no generic sans applied without typographic intent.
